business_problem: In its mission to innovate aluminium to make modern life possible, Emirates Global Aluminium (EGA) needs sustainable, scalable computing infrastructure that its on-premises environment struggled to deliver.
solution_summary: Emirates Global Aluminium modernized its analytics estate on Azure Local, Azure Arc, Azure Databricks, moving from fragmented legacy tooling to a governed cloud data platform. Operational, enterprise, or sensor data is ingested into a shared cloud store and transformed with Azure engineering services so teams can work from one current source of truth. Through its hybrid Azure environment, EGA has achieved 10 to 13 times faster AI response time, 86% cost savings for AI image and video use cases, and several sustainability successes. The architecture emphasizes managed services, reusable integrations, and governed data handling so the organization can scale adoption without rebuilding the solution for each new team or use case.

solution_components.name: Azure Local
solution_components.role: Runs private-cloud workloads close to operations while remaining aligned with Azure tooling.

solution_components.name: Azure Arc
solution_components.role: Applies unified governance and management across hybrid cloud resources.

solution_components.name: Azure Databricks
solution_components.role: Transforms large-scale data and runs analytical or machine-learning workloads.

solution_components.name: Microsoft Copilot
solution_components.role: Provides generative assistance inside end-user productivity workflows.

solution_components.name: Power Platform
solution_components.role: Provides the low-code automation and application platform for workflow modernization.

data_flow: Data flows from operational systems through source-system connectors into the platform data layer, where Azure Databricks prepares and enriches it; business applications then exposes governed analytics and decision support to end users.

EGA moved one-third of its servers to Microsoft Azure and another third to Azure Local as it taps into edge capabilities for safety-critical applications and new industrial AI use cases.
It monitors both sides of the environment with Azure Arc and avoids reengineering solutions as it moves between the public and private cloud.
